headline: Port Hedland Talks Stall at an Iron-Ore Chokepoint
deck: Forecast: BHP and unions ended their latest bargaining round without agreement, keeping Port Hedland on a Tuesday return clock.
body: BHP and unions representing workers at Port Hedland ended their latest bargaining round without an agreement, and the talks are due back before the Fair Work Commission next Tuesday [E1]. Reuters says BHP's updated four-year offer would raise most workers' pay by 17%, add a A$25,000 transition payment over two years and lift roster allowances [E1]. The record is a failed negotiating round, not a declared outage [E1].

A July 31 ABC Western Australia report on the earlier dispute said the unions had already given BHP notice of a 24-hour strike in Port Hedland [E2]. That earlier reporting shows the bargaining had already moved into an industrial sequence with notice and deadlines, but it still was about notice rather than execution [E2]. The new Reuters file confirms the current step is still negotiation, not a stoppage [E1][E2].

Port Hedland remains the physical hinge because Reuters says BHP ships about $80 million of iron ore a day through the operation [E1]. That scale is what makes the site sensitive to even selective action. A wage dispute elsewhere would not carry the same throughput risk [E1].

The current reporting still leaves the mechanism open. It does not establish whether train receival, stockyard blending, shiploading or berth continuity would be the first point of pressure [E1]. It also does not show whether BHP has enough redundancy to keep shipments moving during a narrow stoppage [E1].

Reuters also describes Port Hedland as the world's largest iron-ore loading port and says Australia ships roughly 900 million tonnes of iron ore a year [E1]. Those numbers explain why the bargaining matters beyond a single site. They do not by themselves prove a supply shock, and the record so far is still an unresolved negotiation plus a return date [E1][E2].

The call is 0.68 that Port Hedland is still shipping iron ore when talks resume next Tuesday [E1][E2]. A protected-action notice or confirmed stoppage before then would break that call, and a settlement would too [E1][E2]. Until one of those clocks moves, the evidence still points to an unresolved bargaining dispute rather than a proved physical break [E1][E2].

dissent.argument: The revision fixes the corroboration floor, but it still does not establish the event the forecast depends on. The body shows failed bargaining and an updated offer; it does not show a strike notice, a stoppage, or a Port Hedland outage. On that evidence the outage read remains a forecast, not a fact, and I do not concur with treating it as settled.
